30055.label: Philemon 1:1
30055.text: Paul, a prisoner for the sake of Christ Jesus, and Timothy, [our] brother, to Phi·leʹmon, our beloved one and fellow worker,

30056.label: Philemon 1:2
30056.text: and to Apʹphi·a, our sister, and to Ar·chipʹpus, our fellow soldier, and to the congregation that is in your house:

30057.label: Philemon 1:3
30057.text: May YOU people have undeserved kindness and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus Christ.

30058.label: Philemon 1:4
30058.text: I always thank my God when I make mention of you in my prayers,

30059.label: Philemon 1:5
30059.text: as I keep hearing of your love and faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the holy ones;

30060.label: Philemon 1:6
30060.text: in order that the sharing of your faith may go into action by your acknowledging of every good thing among us as related to Christ.

30061.label: Philemon 1:7
30061.text: For I got much joy and comfort over your love, because the tender affections of the holy ones have been refreshed through you, brother.

30062.label: Philemon 1:8
30062.text: For this very reason, though I have great freeness of speech in connection with Christ to order you to do what is proper,

30063.label: Philemon 1:9
30063.text: I am exhorting you rather on the basis of love, seeing that I am such as I am, Paul an aged man, yes, now also a prisoner for the sake of Christ Jesus;

30064.label: Philemon 1:10
30064.text: I am exhorting you concerning my child, to whom I became a father while in my [prison] bonds, O·nesʹi·mus,

30065.label: Philemon 1:11
30065.text: formerly useless to you but now useful to you and to me.

30066.label: Philemon 1:12
30066.text: This very one I am sending back to you, yes, him, that is, my own tender affections.

30067.label: Philemon 1:13
30067.text: I would like to hold him back for myself that in place of you he might keep on ministering to me in the [prison] bonds I bear for the sake of the good news.

30068.label: Philemon 1:14
30068.text: But without your consent I do not want to do anything, so that your good act may be, not as under compulsion, but of your own free will.

30069.label: Philemon 1:15
30069.text: Perhaps really on this account he broke away for an hour, that you may have him back forever,

30070.label: Philemon 1:16
30070.text: no longer as a slave but as more than a slave, as a brother beloved, especially so to me, yet how much more so to you both in fleshly relationship and in [the] Lord.

30071.label: Philemon 1:17
30071.text: If, therefore, you consider me a sharer, receive him kindly the way you would me.

30072.label: Philemon 1:18
30072.text: Moreover, if he did you any wrong or owes you anything, keep this charged to my account.

30073.label: Philemon 1:19
30073.text: I Paul am writing with my own hand: I will pay it back—not to be telling you that, besides, you owe me even yourself.

30074.label: Philemon 1:20
30074.text: Yes, brother, may I derive profit from you in connection with [the] Lord: refresh my tender affections in connection with Christ.

30075.label: Philemon 1:21
30075.text: Trusting in your compliance, I am writing you, knowing you will even do more than the things I say.

30076.label: Philemon 1:22
30076.text: But along with that, also get lodging ready for me, for I am hoping that through the prayers of YOU people I shall be set at liberty for YOU.

30077.label: Philemon 1:23
30077.text: Sending you greetings is Epʹa·phras my fellow captive in union with Christ,

30078.label: Philemon 1:24
30078.text: [also] Mark, Ar·is·tarʹchus, Deʹmas, Luke, my fellow workers.

30079.label: Philemon 1:25
30079.text: The undeserved kindness of the Lord Jesus Christ [be] with the spirit YOU people [show].
